script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Meta just admitted its big climate promise might not survive the AI boom. Back in twenty twenty, Meta promised to reach net zero emissions by twenty thirty. Now its brand new sustainability report says the company is re-evaluating that goal. Why? Meta's net carbon footprint jumped forty five percent in just one year. That's eleven point nine million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent. Yikes! The culprit is AI. Electricity use rose thirty five percent, driven by new data centers. Compare the rivals: Google up eighteen percent, Amazon up sixteen, Microsoft up twenty five. Meta is the first of those four giants to say it may move its climate timelines. Its own executives put it simply: the reality has been far more complex. Meta says it has contracted more than thirty gigawatts of clean energy, from nuclear, solar and geothermal. But less than half of that is actually producing electricity so far. A contract can't spin a turbine! So when utilities can't deliver power fast enough, Meta says it may turn to natural gas plants. In Louisiana, Entergy is pursuing seven new gas units, over five thousand megawatts, for Meta's data centers. One bright spot: direct water use fell four percent, but use in water-stressed regions rose twenty four percent. Meta gave no date for a decision. It only promised to share where this work lands. Smarter AI, hotter planet? Read the full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net!
